result.title: Fragment-Level Graph Encoding for Interpretable Molecular Property Prediction
result.comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, 6-page appendices, to be published in Proceedings of the 8th Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference (NLDL), 2027. For associated code, see https://github.com/4D-Lab/frame
result.summary: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are among the standard tools for molecular property prediction, but the atom-level explanations of their predictions are hard for medicinal chemists to act on. We propose a change of input representation rather than a new model: molecules are encoded as fragment-level graphs from BRICS decomposition, where each node is a synthetically meaningful fragment whose features are the element-wise sum of its atoms' features. Because only the representation changes, any message-passing GNN and any post-hoc attribution method produces explanations at the resolution of functional groups instead of single atoms. Across four architectures, four prediction tasks, and two explainers under scaffold splits, fragment-level encoding matches atom-level test accuracy on roughly five-fold smaller graphs. Integrated-Gradients attributions recover known pharmacophores above chance on two enzyme targets, namely BACE at 1.5 times the chance rate, and PTR1 at 3.2 times. A like-for-like comparison against an aggregated atom-level baseline shows that post-hoc aggregation is not a stable substitute: its BACE hit rate range both exceeds and falls below the fragment model's hit rate depending on two arbitrary aggregation choices, whereas fragment-level training yields a single convention-free attribution at no predictive cost. The code is available at: https://github.com/4D-Lab/frame

AI.brief_summary: 论文不设计新模型，而把分子改编码为 BRICS 片段级图（节点特征为所属原子特征逐元素求和），在四种 GNN、四个任务与两种解释器下比较片段级与原子级表示的预测精度与归因可解释性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「只改输入单元粒度、不改模型」以及事后聚合原子归因依赖任意约定而不稳定的分析，可能为 LVR 中视觉 token 粒度选择、证据归因与视觉旁路核查提供类比线索，可供核查。
